A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the risk of death from any cause, from breast cancer and from cardiovascular disease was higher in women who gained weight or had weight fluctuations after their breast cancer diagnosis than it was in women who maintained or lost weight.
post-diagnosis weight gain is a significant risk factor for mortality, and that weight gain is associated with increased mortality risk in breast cancer survivors.
weight gain after breast cancer diagnosis was associated with an increased risk of mortality from all causes and specifically breast cancer and cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast cancer patients who gained weight had an increased mortality risk, especially from breast cancer and cardiovascular disease, compared to patients who maintained or lost weight.

breast cancer survivors who gain weight after their diagnosis have a higher risk of dying from breast cancer, and that survivors who gain a lot of weight after diagnosis have a particularly high risk of dying from cardiovascular disease.

weight gain after breast cancer diagnosis is associated with increased all-cause mortality, and that this association is not limited to women who were overweight or obese before breast cancer diagnosis.
